discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 181735
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1235 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very mild this week with highs in the low to mid 60s Wednesday 
  through Saturday.

- Rain chances hold off until Sunday (20-60% chances).

- Mild weather pattern persists at least through the end of
  November.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1234 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

A large upper level ridge continues to amplify into the Midwest and 
Great Lakes regions with the dry and very mild weather pattern 
expected to last through this week. Surface high pressure will 
prevail with litle movement from where it is anchored over the 
Appalachian mountains. Southerly flow and increased WAA will funnel 
in much warmer air from the Gulf and southern US. There are no 
hazardous weather concerns this week as both high and low 
temperatures will continue to climb well above seasonal averages. 
High temperatures will soar into the low to mid 60s starting 
tomorrow, which will be 15 to 20 degrees above normal for this 
time of the year! Lows will be above freezing in the 40s. Friday
and Saturday will be the warmest days of the week, with near 
record high temperatures.

As the ridge breaks down by late in the week, rain chances return on 
Sunday as a cold front moves through. Compared to yesterday, models 
have slowed down the timing of this front into our area by about 12 
hours; wheras before it looked like we could get some scattered 
showers Saturday night, now it appears like Saturday will stay dry 
and Sunday now has the bulk of the rain chances. By the time it 
makes its way into our forecast area, the cold front should be 
fairly weak. With a limited amount of instability and potentially 
unfavorable morning timing to work with, only light rainfall amounts 
of 0.10-0.25" are anticipated on Sunday. Have maintained low to 
medium PoPs on Sunday with 20-40% chances. Following the frontal 
passage, temperatures will moderate back towards seasonable levels 
with highs in the 40s. There are no real signs of winter yet as the 
mild weather pattern looks to hold at least through the end of 
meteorological fall. 

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 1102 AM EST Wed Nov 18 2026

Dry and stable air mass on the western periphery of high
pressure will allow VFR conditions, southerly winds up to near
10 knots and mainly clear skies to persist through the TAF 
cycle.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Johnson
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.text:
SPC AC 181622

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1022 AM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

   Valid 181630Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the contiguous U.S.
   through tonight.

   ...Florida Peninsula...
   A convective complex/MCV will continue to move slowly
   south-southeastward over the FL Straits this afternoon as a weak
   mid-level low persists over the Southeast/northern Gulf. This
   activity should gradually trend away from the Keys and southern FL
   Peninsula, but transient low-level circulations may persist over
   nearshore waters for a bit longer. The latest KAMX/KBYX VWPs show
   modestly enhanced easterly winds around 1-2 km AGL in the presence
   of a very moist low-level airmass and convectively reinforced
   baroclinic zone. While a waterspout/occasional strong thunderstorm
   could occur near coastal areas, a continued offshore drift to the
   parent MCV and weak mid-level flow should limit organized severe
   potential over land.

   Farther north across the eastern FL Peninsula, modest low-level
   easterly flow will continue to transport a moist low-level airmass
   inland along the Atlantic Coast. But, poor mid-level lapse rates and
   generally modest winds in the 850-500 mb layer noted in the observed
   12Z MFL/TBW soundings will likely hinder updraft intensity and
   overall severe threat with any convection that develops this
   afternoon and evening.

   ...California...
   An upper trough/low centered off the coastal Pacific Northwest and
   northern CA will approach the West Coast by tonight, with an
   inland-moving front and a strong, cyclonically curved mid-level jet
   developing from CA toward the Great Basin. A post-frontal/diurnal
   steepening of low/mid-level lapse rates will support isolated
   thunderstorm potential initially focused near coastal northern CA
   this afternoon, and expanding to include central/interior CA tonight
   through early Thursday morning. While occasional strong/gusty winds
   could occur with this convection, instability should remain too
   limited to support an appreciable severe risk.

   ..Gleason/Halbert-E.. 11/18/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 181711

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1111 AM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

   Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS WITHIN THE SAN
   JOAQUIN VALLEY VICINITY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms are possible over portions
   of the San Joaquin Valley vicinity with a brief tornado or two and
   isolated damaging gusts possible Thursday afternoon.

   ...Synopsis...
   A deep upper low will move into northern California and the Great
   Basin on Thursday. The mid-level jet will primarily impact southern
   California, but moderate mid-level westerlies will extend as far
   north as the San Joaquin Valley. A surface low associated with the
   upper-level trough will move into the Bay Area during the early
   morning hours. A cold front will extend southwestward from this
   surface low. The front will sweep eastward through the afternoon,
   reaching central/eastern portions of the Great Basin by Friday
   morning.

   ...San Joaquin Valley Vicinity...
   Precipitation is likely to be ongoing during the early morning hours
   due to moderate to strong warm advection and mid-level ascent. In
   the wake of this activity, muted surface heating and very cold
   temperatures aloft (around -25 C at 500 mb) will lead to weak
   destabilization within the Valley. Terrain-enhanced southerly winds
   within the Valley will promote sufficient low-level shear that, when
   coupled with the stronger westerlies aloft, will promote some risk
   for marginal supercell structures. The strongest, most organized
   storms could produce a brief tornado or two during early to mid
   afternoon. Flow in the lowest 2-3 km will not be particularly strong
   and will be weakening through the afternoon. Even so, isolated
   damaging wind gusts are possible, particularly within the higher
   terrain areas.

   ..Wendt.. 11/18/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 180830

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

   Valid 201200Z - 211200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Friday.

   ...Central/Northern Rockies and Plains States...
   An upper trough over the Great basin is forecast to eject eastward
   across the Rockies and into the northern/central Plains as it merges
   with a second weaker perturbation emanating from southern Canada.
   Strong southwesterly flow aloft will overspread the Plains states
   deepening a lee cyclone across eastern CO/WY. This will draw modest
   surface moisture northward ahead of a cold front/lee trough tied to
   the low. Strong ascent ahead of the aforementioned trough and
   boundaries, along with the modest moisture return may support
   isolated thunderstorms across the Plains late Friday afternoon into
   early Saturday. While deep-layer flow will strengthen through the
   day, relatively cool surface temperatures and overall modest
   buoyancy suggests severe potential will be quite limited. Additional
   isolated storms are possible under the core of the upper trough
   throughout the higher terrain.

   ...Gulf and Atlantic Coasts...
   A weak upper trough will move from the eastern Gulf across the FL
   peninsula Friday. A broad low over open waters farther west should
   gradually fill while a compact secondary surface low is forecast to
   deepen along the Atlantic coast. Weak ascent fro the upper trough
   will support scattered thunderstorms within a moist and broad yet
   weakly unstable environment from the middle Gulf Coast to FL. Poor
   lapse rates and generally weak upper-level flow should preclude much
   in the way of storm organization. However, given scattered storm
   coverage, sporadic damaging gusts is possible.

   ..Lyons.. 11/18/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
